scope: Proposition 7.5 (Uniform stage bounds) of the manuscript “Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three” (preprints/Absolutely-Continuous-Spectrum-for-Weak-Disorder-Anderson-Models-in-Dimensions-at-Least-Three-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0d971c56f6ba1641), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the fixed energy window and the initial- ization constants as in Proposition 3.6. For sufficiently large n0, uniformly in m ≥ 4n0 and in the fixed energy in that window, the following statements hold along every finite history produced by the ordinary-sweep and clearing rules, with failed trials rolled back. At each com- pleted stage start the diagonal fixed-point relation, the three comparisons (7), the fourth-row bound maxi P j |hij|4 ≤ t1+δ, and ∥K∥ ≤ 1/3 hold. The vectors r remain bounded with their imaginary parts in one fixed positive bounded range. The low comparison constants remain in fixed positive bounded ranges, and the rough high constant C0 can be chosen independently of the stage. The kernel of D consists of the constants, at least N/2 sites remain active, and the terminal metric satisfies (128). During a clearing stage, every committed prestate has lag o(t.36δ), fourth-row sums below .8t1+δ, and the comparison bounds furnished by Proposition 7.3. No comparison for D or bound on K is asserted at a provisional heat prefix. All constants and smallness thresholds are independent of the history and of the torus volume.
